transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brings me in is that my eating has just gotten really off lately. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before my shift. And I've noticed my scrubs have been hanging pretty loose on me, even though I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. I just don't have much of an appetite right now.
Aside from your appetite changes, how has your mood been lately?

Honestly, it hasn't been great. Most mornings, I just wake up with this... heavy, hollow feeling. It's like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. I've just been feeling really down.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, the steady depression and... just the loss of interest in things, that settled in a bit later. I'd say it has been with me for roughly the past year and four months now.
Before this past year and four months, have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling down or losing interest in things?

No, not really. Before this past year and a half, I didn't have these kinds of long stretches where I felt so low. And I should clarify, for most of this whole stretch—this past year and four months—I’ve been living with that heavy, hollow mood and loss of interest pretty much constantly. It’s not just having a few bad weeks here and there. It's been a steady thing.
How has your sleep been during this time?

It's been pretty bad, honestly. My sleep is just... broken up. I usually lie in bed replaying everything that happened at work, and I find myself just listening for noises. Then, when I do manage to drop off, I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. Once I'm awake, I just can't seem to settle back down before my alarm goes off.
You mentioned replaying what happened at work—did you experience or witness an event involving severe danger, serious injury, or a threat to life?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I work in healthcare support, so it gets stressful, but... no, I haven't been in any kind of extreme danger or seen a life-threatening event or anything. 

When I say I'm replaying things, it's more just... regular work stuff. Like, worrying if I forgot a task during my shift, or thinking about a conversation with a coworker that felt a little off. It's just normal day-to-day things, really, but my brain just won't let them go when I'm trying to sleep.
How have your energy levels been throughout the day during this time?

Honestly, my energy is just gone. Even if I spend the whole night in bed, my body feels like I just finished a double shift. It's just this heavy exhaustion right from the start of the day. And by the time lunchtime rolls around, I'm really fighting just to keep my thoughts together and keep moving.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt the complete opposite—unusually energetic, elated, or full of energy despite needing very little sleep?

No, I haven't. I've never had anything like that. It's really just been this low, heavy feeling. I don't think I've ever felt unusually energetic or like I didn't need sleep. If anything, I just always feel like I need more rest, even when I can't get it.
With everything feeling so heavy, have you had any thoughts that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I haven't... I haven't made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But, um... I do catch myself just wishing I wouldn't wake up in the morning. Or just thinking that it would be so much easier if I could just disappear. It's not that I want to do something to myself, it's just... I'm so tired, and sometimes not being here just seems like it would be easier.
